about: Appearance research schema (2026-10-21): what is asked of a model about one building from street-level Mapillary frames. Every attribute allows 'cannot_tell', and saying so is a correct answer when the photo does not show it. v2 (2026-10-22): style replaced by three independent axes (era, form, material), and shops simplified to none/some/all, because the v1 style menu's entries overlapped (shop-and-flats is Edwardian flats over shops) and most 'errors' were between neighbouring entries.

usable.says: yes only if the building between the red dashed lines (the target) is clearly visible: most of its street wall, at least its ground floor and its full height (a one-storey building is fine), not mostly hidden by trees, vehicles, scaffolding or another building

storeys.says: floors above the street on the target's street wall, counting the ground floor

shops.says: ground-floor shopfronts (display windows, shop doors, signage) on the visible street wall: none; some (one or a few, the rest is entrance, garage or wall); all (the whole ground floor is shops)

awnings.says: fabric or metal awnings or canopies over the ground floor

balconies.says: balconettes = shallow railings at windows (Juliet balconies, iron rails); balconies = platforms you can stand on that project from the wall

bay_windows.says: windows that project out from the wall as a box or angled bay, on upper floors

fire_escape.says: metal fire escape stairs/landings on the visible street wall

main_colour.says: the main wall colour, ignoring windows, signs and the ground floor if it is painted differently; a shaded white wall is still white

says.victorian: 1870-1905: ornate wood trim, tall narrow windows, slanted bay windows, gables or false fronts, brackets
says.edwardian: 1905-1925: square or rounded bays, classical cornice, simpler trim, flats and apartment blocks of that age, brick and terracotta commercial
says.interwar: 1925-1945: stucco, Mediterranean/Spanish/Deco/Streamline, arches, tile, garage under
says.postwar: 1945-1985: plain boxes, aluminium or ribbon windows, flat fronts, little ornament
says.recent: 1985-today: panels, large glass, box bays, contemporary materials

says.house: a single house or a pair of flats of 1-3 storeys
says.flats: a small residential building of 2-4 storeys with several flats (several doors or bells, bay stacks)
says.commercial: shops, offices, warehouse or workshop, no homes visible above
